newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen steady at open, bonds guide trade.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen steady at open, bonds guide trade.

text.p: Wall Street markets were seen opening flat to slightly higher in quiet trading on Thursday, with bonds providing market direction in the absence of fresh economic data to inspire share prices.

The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off about 0.10 points at 842.75, firming from earlier lows as bonds were unchanged after the release of U.S. jobless claims data for the week ended May 17. Claims were 322,000 in the week versus a revised 317,000 in the prior week.
"The market should open relatively flat," Dan Ascani, president of Global Market Strategists Inc, said.
The long bond was trading off 6/32 at a 6.98 percent yield compared with yesterday's yield of 6.96 percent.
Ascani said the jobless data did not show a strong increase in claims and might be viewed by markets as slightly favorable after last week's number.
Other analysts predicted stocks would open higher after the Dow industrials pared losses late in Wednesday's session. Losses were caused by profit-taking and weaker bonds.
Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said good news about a tobacco ruling in Maryland could boost cigarette-maker shares, and the Dow industrials.
